The following parameters define thresholds and differentials used in positional correlation calculations for track association, with specific rules governing their application:

- **c = 7 (range: 3–7, step: 1)** — “Min TQ”. This is the minimum Track Quality (TQ) value permitted in positional correlation calculations. Any TQ lower than c shall be treated as if it were equal to c. This constraint prevents correlation windows from becoming unrealistically large. Note: The value assigned to c must never be less than or equal to the value assigned to e.

- **d = 10 (range: 8–15, step: 1)** — “Max TQ”. This is the maximum TQ value permitted in positional correlation calculations. Any TQ higher than d shall be treated as if it were equal to d. This constraint prevents correlation windows from becoming unrealistically small.

- **e = 4 (range: 2–6, step: 1)** — “Restricted TQ”. Tracks with a TQ less than or equal to e are not eligible for correlation, except for new local real-time tracks (as specified in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f(1)(a) and 4.4.4.3.1f(4)).

- **f = 45 degrees (range: 15–90, step: 15)** — “Course Differential”. This defines the maximum allowable difference between the reported course of a remote track and the calculated course of a local track for correlation to be considered valid. If the speed of either track is less than 10 decameters per hour (dmh), the course differential criterion shall not be applied in the correlation test.

- **g = 40 percent (range: 10–100, step: 10)** — “Speed Differential”. This specifies the maximum percentage by which the speed of the faster track may differ from the speed of the slower track for correlation to be allowed.

- **h = 10 thousand feet (kft) (range: 5–50, step: 5)** — “Altitude Differential”. This sets the maximum allowable altitude difference between two air tracks for correlation to be permitted. This parameter is not applicable to surface track correlation.

- **j = 2 (range: 1–5, step: 1)** — “Min Qpg”. This is the minimum value of Qpg (position quality factor) to be used in positional correlation calculations. Any Qpg value lower than j shall be treated as if it were equal to j. This prevents correlation windows used in testing correlation of PPLI (Precise Position Location Information) positions from becoming unrealistically large.

- **k = 11 (range: 1–15, step: 1)** — “Max Qpg”. This is the maximum value of Qpg to be used in positional correlation calculations. Any Qpg value higher than k shall be treated as if it were equal to k. This prevents correlation windows used in testing correlation of PPLI positions from becoming unrealistically small.
